title: The flashcard whose front side is never the same sentence twice
claim: Intermediate self-learners stall on listening not because their vocabulary is too small but because the example sentence on the card is fixed — what they have memorised is the card, not the sound of the word.
method: HN Algolia full-text search for wish/there-is-no-app phrasings, then read the full comment tree of 'A love letter to flashcards' (206 points / 116 comments, 2026-07-10) and pulled verbatim quotes. Cross-read old.reddit across five subreddit clusters (learning-a-craft, parenting, small-business, decluttering) with four phrasings; 'Reaching C1 is depressing' (329 points) corroborates the population size. Product Hunt API scanned from 2026-07-18 to confirm nobody is shipping this.
hook: An adult who has drilled Anki daily for years, reads N3 text fine, and still cannot follow N4 speech. They know the drilling is not working and they have already hand-rolled a workaround (sentence mining) rather than wait for a product.
does: Import a word list you already have. Every review generates a sentence for that word you have never seen before, synthesised to audio. The audio plays first — you decide whether you understood it — and only after you answer is the text revealed.
edge: The practice material is generated fresh each review, so you can never memorise the card instead of the word; and audio precedes text, which kills the illusion the learner described in his own words.
why_use: It does not ask you to change your habit. You keep the same daily review slot and the same word list; only the front of the card changes.
pain: You have put in years. You can read the language. You put on a drama and understand nothing. Every app tells you your streak is intact.
gap: A static SRS deck gives a word one or two example sentences for life. Generating a new natural sentence plus new audio on every single review was not structurally possible before generative models; the community's workaround, sentence mining, is people doing this by hand, one card at a time.
counter: The real cause is probably raw input volume, not card format — an N2-level speaker in the same thread says flatly that spaced repetition will not help you hear, and that the fix is listening to actual conversations. Unnatural AI sentences are fatal here and it is a fresh bet on every single review. And the moat is thin: Anki plus a TTS add-on plus a generation plugin gets you 80% of the way, with Migaku and Kamesame already in the lane.
kill: One stilted sentence and a Japanese learner is gone; the spacing algorithm itself carries no value (a commenter in the same thread puts it at 'just 100 lines of python'); Anki's plugin ecosystem can absorb this as a feature.
differentiator: Not another SRS. The only difference is that the front of the card stops being fixed material and becomes freshly generated listening material, with audio forced ahead of text. Cold start — Chinese: Xiaohongshu and Bilibili N3-listening and shadowing self-study bloggers, with one-click import from MOJi辞書 and Hujiang word lists. English: reply directly under that HN comment, then r/LearnJapanese and r/languagelearning sentence-mining threads, with the Anki add-on marketplace as the distribution channel.
move: Ship one language, one word list format, one screen. Reply to the HN commenter with a working link before building anything else.
value: Turns the review slot the learner already keeps into a daily dose of fresh, real context, so listening actually grows with review.
risk: Sentence naturalness below par destroys trust immediately; narrow differentiation from Migaku and Kamesame; absorbable by Anki as a plugin.
consumer_angle: Ordinary adults teaching themselves Japanese, Spanish or French in their own time. The artefact they get is a fresh piece of listening practice every day, built from the words they personally got wrong.
voices: For language learning, I wish there was an audio-first flashcard app that changes up the example sentences every time. Right now, I'm using Anki to learn Japanese vocabulary from N5 to N3. I know the words and the example sentences well enough to read N3-level text, provided I know the grammar. But when it comes to listening, I struggle to understand even N4-level spoken Japanese. Anki just doesn't offer enough variety for me to truly internalize what the sound means in different contexts. Plus, seeing the text before hearing the audio tricks my brain. I think I'm learning the sound, but it's an illusion because I already know the meaning from seeing the word first.
Audio first is an interesting idea. As a fluent speaker who's always felt ashamed of his poor writing skills that's actually something that I would want as well.
This is a big part of why language learners have largely moved toward sentence mining as the preferred way to build an Anki deck.
despite practicing everyday I wonder and question am I even progressing? ... I wish there was a way to 2XP speed boost this journey, been doing this already for long enough

zh.title: 正面永远不是同一句话的那张记忆卡
zh.claim: 中高级外语自学者卡在听力，不是词汇量不够，而是卡片的例句是固定的——他们记住的是那张卡片，不是那个词的声音。
zh.hook: 刷了几年 Anki、读得动 N3 文章、放一部日剧还是一句听不懂的成年人。他知道这么背没用，而且已经自己动手绕过去了（sentence mining），没等产品。
zh.does: 导入你已有的词表。每次复习都为该词现生成一条你从没见过的例句并合成语音；先只播音频，你判断听懂没有，答对之后才揭示文字。
zh.edge: 练习素材每次现生成，你没机会把卡片背下来冒充背会了词；音频先于文字，直接掐掉学习者自己说的那个错觉。
zh.why_use: 不要求你改习惯。还是那个每天的复习时段、还是那份词表，只换卡片正面。
zh.pain: 你投入了好几年，字能读，剧一放什么都听不懂，而所有 app 都在告诉你连续打卡没断。
zh.gap: 静态牌组里一个词一辈子只有那一两句例句。每次复习都现生成一条自然的新句子加新配音，在生成式模型出现之前结构上做不到；社区的绕法 sentence mining，就是人在一张一张手工做这件事。
zh.counter: 真因大概率是输入总量不够而不是卡片形式——同帖一位 N2 水平的人直接说 spaced repetition 帮不了你听懂，真解法是大量真实对话。AI 例句不自然在这里是致命的，而且每次复习都要重新赌一次。护城河也薄：Anki 加 TTS 插件加一个生成插件就有八成，Migaku、Kamesame 已在同一赛道。
zh.differentiator: 不做又一个 SRS。唯一差异是把卡片正面从固定素材变成每次现生成的新鲜听力素材，并强制音频先于文字。冷启动——中文：小红书与 B 站的 N3 听力、shadowing 自学博主，配 MOJi辞書与沪江词单一键导入；英文：直接回复 HN 那条评论，再进 r/LearnJapanese 与 r/languagelearning 的 sentence mining 帖，用 Anki 插件市场做分发。
zh.value: 把学习者本来就在花的复习时间，变成每天一段新鲜的真实语境。
zh.risk: 例句自然度不达标即刻失信；与 Migaku、Kamesame 差异窄；可能被 Anki 以插件形式吸收。
